features.name: mean_opening_paragraph_words
features.definition: What is the average number of words in the opening paragraph of the counter-argument comments?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of strings; if missing/malformed return null; if empty list return null (no comments to average). For each comment (string), strip leading/trailing whitespace, split on blank lines using re.split(r'\n\s*\n', text), take the first nonempty segment as the opening paragraph, and count words with len(re.findall(r"\b\w+(?:['’-]\w+)*\b", para)). Skip comments that are empty after stripping. Return the mean of these counts across the remaining comments; null if none remain. Raw text counting; no semantic filtering.

h0: mean_opening_paragraph_words has no association with the probability the OP changed their view (delta).
h1: Lower mean_opening_paragraph_words is associated with a higher probability of delta (negative coefficient).
note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP view change). Opening paragraph is the first blank-line-separated block of each comment; comments lacking paragraph breaks count entirely as the opening paragraph. Row-level aggregate is the mean across comments in OC_comments (list order carries no meaning); this measures the row's comments, not individual comment persuasiveness, since no per-comment outcomes exist. Word count is raw text, so quoted text or edits/outcome announcements within a comment may be included. Association only, not causal.
